answer: Escrowed reputation decay: each new identity must post a small refundable deposit that decays only through verified interactions, so value accrues like a river carving a channel rather than a one-time toll. Every deposit creates a ripple across linked accounts, since shared funding sources or timing patterns trigger proportional escrow increases for the whole cluster. An attacker who wants to wander across thousands of fake identities must pre-fund each one and wait out decay, so marginal cost per identity rises with cluster size instead of staying flat.
